title: The Appeal to Ignorance Fallacy Every Smart Person Should Know About
tags: appeal to ignorance logical fallacy examples
description:
Have you ever heard someone say, “You can’t prove me wrong, so I must be right”? That’s the Appeal to Ignorance fallacy in action. Also called argumentum ad ignorantiam, this logical fallacy happens when people claim something is true simply because it hasn’t been proven false—or false because it hasn’t been proven true. From creationists denying evolution, to conspiracy theorists saying the moon landing was faked, to theists claiming God must exist because you can’t disprove it—this fallacy shows up everywhere.

In this video, Pale Blue Thoughts breaks down the Appeal to Ignorance fallacy with real-world examples from homeopathy, religion, conspiracy theories, ghosts, psychic powers, and intelligent design arguments. We’ll also explain Bertrand Russell’s famous teapot analogy, why the burden of proof lies on the claimant, and how absence of evidence is not evidence of absence. If you’ve searched for logical fallacies explained, Appeal to Ignorance examples, burden of proof, argument from ignorance, or how to debate pseudoscience, this video gives you the rational perspective.
